subject: Recap + proposed PoC tests: dedicated capacity vs cloud bursting
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara@nimbus-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-14T15:02:00Z
Subject: Recap: capacity & performance discussion — next test proposal

Hi Sara — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a concrete PoC proposal so we can align on scope and timing.

Call highlights (what we heard)
- Traffic profile: intermittent bursts with long tails; expected steady-state 40–60k tokens/min, peak bursts up to ~150k tokens/min for short windows.
- Latency target: p95 around ~80ms for user-facing generation paths.
- Risk areas for you: preemptible instances on public clouds causing interruption, cold-starts on scale-up, regional quotas and capacity guarantees, regulatory boundary for PHI-ish data.

How Redwood differentiates (brief)
- Dedicated pools: reserved GPU capacity with predictable scheduling and isolation (no preemption).
- Deterministic latency: runtime optimizations (prefix cache + continuous batching) to hit p95 SLOs under steady load.
- Smart routing: automatic fallback to compatible model variants in other regions when capacity constrained.
- Cost controls: burst credits + autoscale policies to limit spend during spikes.

Proposed PoC test plan (3 targeted runs)
1) Sustained throughput run — 24-hour steady load at 60k tokens/min to validate thermal/throughput stability and cost per token. Collect latency p50/p95, GPU utilization, and per-token cost.
2) Burst & failover test — simulate abrupt 10x short burst and then a regional outage to validate cross-region fallback and model-variant routing. Measure end-to-end latency impact and request loss.
3) Cost parity microbench — run identical model (same weights, same batch/config) on Redwood Dedicated vs. equivalent hyperscaler reserved GPU instances to compare cost-per-token and tail latency under identical request mixes.

Deliverables we’ll provide
- PoC test plan (attached stub) with exact request traces and test harness config (we can drive load from your env or ours).
- A short pricing summary for a two-week dedicated pilot and reserved commitment options.
- Security quicksheet covering network isolation, KMS integration, and audit logs for SOC/HIPAA questions.

Questions for you
- Are these three tests aligned with your evaluation criteria? Any additions/constraints (e.g., must be run inside your VPC)?
- Preferred kickoff window (we suggested 2026-06-01, but flexible).
- Any procurement/PO steps we should loop in now?

Attachments: PoC-test-plan-v1.pdf (test steps + harness), summary.xlsx referenced below.

Next step: if you agree, we’ll lock dates, provision a small dedicated pool for the pilot (10–20 concurrent workers) and share runbooks.

Thanks — Karthik

1) Reserved pricing: can you share the per-GPU committed pricing (and what the minimum term is) vs the pilot pricing?
2) Region outage behavior: in your bullet you mentioned fallback to other regions — what guarantees do you provide for stateful workloads (user session cache / KV)?

We also need a short security summary for our infosec — HIPAA-like controls are required for this project.

Karthik / Vivek — quick internal notes on the proposed PoC:
- Tests look good. Add a 4th validation: model-variant fallback behavior under scale-down (ensure no request corruption and acceptable latency delta).
- Pricing offer: recommend we propose a two-week dedicated pilot with a 10% pilot discount and SLA: 99.9% for the pilot window (operationally we can commit).
- For region outage test, include a run that exercises cross-region KV replication (we need to confirm if the prospect wants warm replication or eventual consistency).
- Security: prepare a 1–2 page quicksheet covering VPC peering, KMS/HSM, audit logs retention, and SOC 2 scope — Sara asked specifically for HIPAA-like controls. I’ll draft an executive note for sales if you want.

I’ll also flag a small promotional credit we can offer if procurement pushes back on cost.

Subject: Re: Recap: capacity & performance discussion — next test proposal

Sara — answers and next steps below.

1) Reserved / pilot pricing
- Two-week dedicated pilot: fixed pilot pool (equivalent of 2 x A40-class GPUs) priced at $X,XXX/week with an introductory 10% discount (total pilot credit applied on invoice). No long-term commitment required for pilot.
- Reserved capacity: 12-month and 36-month options. Per-GPU committed pricing and commitment tiers attached in dedicated-pricing-summary.xlsx.

2) Region outage & stateful guarantees
- By default we will route traffic to a compatible model instance in another region when local capacity is depleted; this is best-effort fallover and will increase latency depending on geography.
- For stateful caches (KV / prefix caches) we offer two modes:
  a) warm cross-region replication (recommended) — keeps a recent copy of KV state replicated to standby region (adds small write latency).
  b) eventual replication — lower cost, higher RTO for cache warmup.
- For the PoC we recommend warm replication for user-facing flows to avoid session inconsistency. We can show measured deltas in the burst/failover test.

3) Support during pilot
- Standard: 9×5 email + pager escalation to on-call engineering.
- Optional: 24×7 phone/Slack support and an assigned Solutions Engineer for $Y,YYY/mo during pilot. We can include SE hours in the pilot price if you want.

Attachments: dedicated-pricing-summary.xlsx, security-quicksheet.pdf

Proposed next steps
- Please confirm you’re good with the three PoC runs + Marissa’s model-variant fallback addition.
- Approve pilot week: target 2026-06-01 start (we’ll reserve capacity this week if you confirm).
- Procurement: if you want, loop in procurement@redwood.ai and I’ll start the SOW/quote.

If that sounds right I’ll send a one-page SOW + a test-run schedule by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — Karthik
